REX DCS: Rapid Extraction Wheeled Rescue Litter with Descent Control
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/rex-one-dcs-multi-purpose-extraction-stretcher-with-descent-control-system
Manufacturer page: https://rapidextraction.com/rex-systems/rex-dcs/
Spec sheet: REX overview brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: rescue litter (150/mo, KD0). Secondary: rope rescue stretcher (0-10), extraction stretcher (0-10), descent control stretcher (0, not indexed), multi purpose extraction stretcher (0). Ricky's note: not-indexed terms are real product language; use them in the copy, but do not expect volume. Also used: stair stretcher (80, from the REX ONE row).
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Rapid Extraction Wheeled Rescue Litter with Descent Control Brake for Stairs – REX DCS
Current H1: REX DCS – Multi-Purpose Extraction Stretcher with Descent Control System
Subtitle: Multi-Purpose Extraction Stretcher and Stair Stretcher with a Hand Brake for Controlled Descent Down Stairwells and Steep Terrain
Current subtitle: Rapid Extraction Rex DCS Patient Evacuation Stretcher with Hand Brake Descent Control Feature
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Rapid Extraction REX DCS is a wheeled rescue litter with a built-in Descent Control System, so one responder can bring a patient down stairwells, steep grades, and rough ground at a controlled speed. It is the REX ONE multi-purpose extraction stretcher with an integrated hand brake, and it still converts into a backboard or a patient treatment cot.
Dual brake rods slow both wheels evenly from a single hand brake lever, and a safety lock button holds the brakes on without constant pressure, so the stretcher does not roll when it is stopped. Safety connection brackets and straps give responders extra control on difficult descents, which makes the REX DCS a practical stair stretcher for high-rise evacuations, mass casualty incidents, and EMS and fire teams.
Descent Control System: Hand brake lever controls speed and braking during descent down stairs and steep terrain
Brakes: Dual rod braking system for even braking in any condition, with a forged alloy dual cable brake lever and heavy duty steel cabling and housing
Brake Lock: Safety lock button keeps the brake rods locked without constant pressure on the hand brake; the emergency brake locking system prevents rolling
Safety Connections: Safety connection brackets and safety straps for additional control
Frame: Rugged T-6 aerospace aluminum with a patented tri-fold panel system
Configurations: Converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or patient treatment cot, and adjusts for supine and Fowler’s positions
Setup: Ready to roll in under 30 seconds
Load Capacity: 400 lbs
Ground Clearance: 10” from the ground to the base
Wheels: Quick-release, airless all-terrain wheel system; the wheels come off for use as a backboard
Maneuverability: 360° turning, with a telescoping pull handle
Headrest: Adjustable locking headrest
Patient Straps: Interchangeable patient restraint straps (set of 3)
Fenders: Protective wheel fenders keep the patient clear of the tires
Includes: Backpack carrying case
Colors: Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
Warranty: 1-year warranty
Country of Manufacture: Made in the U.S.A.
Available Models and Options
REX DCS – Standard Tires: Airless all-terrain tires; Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
Accessories: Bike tow attachment (tow bar and hitch) and removable IV pole
[H2] Uses
The REX DCS suits teams that need to move patients down the stairs or steep ground with fewer responders.
Typical uses include:
High-rise and multi-story evacuation: Bring patients down stairwells when the elevators cannot be used
Steep grades and rough terrain: Controlled descent on hillsides, embankments, and trails
EMS and fire departments: One responder can move a patient from the scene to the ambulance
Mass casualty incidents and medical surge: One responder per patient frees others for patient care
Hospitals and care facilities: Evacuate non-ambulatory patients down the stairs
Bike patrols and events: With the bike tow attachment, a bike team can tow the stretcher across large sites
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
How does the descent control brake work?
Squeeze the hand brake lever to slow both wheels through the dual brake rods. Press the safety lock button to hold the brakes on without keeping pressure on the lever.
Can one responder take a patient down the stairs?
Yes. The REX DCS is designed for a single responder, and the hand brake controls the speed on the way down. The safety connection brackets and straps let a second responder add control on difficult descents.
How is the REX DCS different from the REX ONE?
The REX DCS has the same tri-fold frame, configurations, and 400 lb capacity as the REX ONE, and adds the Descent Control System brake for stairs and steep terrain.
Is the REX DCS a rescue litter?
Yes, a wheeled one. Unlike a basket litter that a team carries, the REX DCS rolls on all-terrain wheels, brakes on the stairs, and folds into a backpack case.
[H2] About Rapid Extraction REX Stretchers
REX stretchers fold in three for compact storage and roll on airless all-terrain wheels, so one responder can move a patient over stairs, rough ground, and long distances.
The REX line includes:
REX ONE: Multi-purpose extraction stretcher that converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or treatment cot
REX DCS: The REX ONE with a Descent Control System hand brake for stairs and steep ground
REX DCS/CF: The REX DCS for correctional facilities, with Humane Restraint cuffs and full body restraint straps
[H2] About Rapid Extraction
Rapid Extraction (REX EMS, LLC) of Glendora, California, designs and builds REX stretchers in the U.S.A., and REX stretchers won an EMS World Innovation Award.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: Ricky's primary keyword "rescue litter" is in the H1, the first sentence, a FAQ, the meta title, and the meta description. The search results for it are basket litters (Stokes baskets, CMC, North American Rescue) plus some animal rescue pages, so I wrote "wheeled rescue litter" and added the FAQ "Is the REX DCS a rescue litter?" to explain the difference. "Extraction stretcher," "multi-purpose extraction stretcher," and "descent control" are used as product language, as Ricky suggested.
Stair stretcher (80/mo, from the REX ONE row): it did not fit the REX ONE, but it fits here, since the REX DCS is the REX model for stairs. I used it in the subtitle, the intro, the meta title, and the meta description. Ricky, please confirm.
"Rope rescue stretcher": Rapid Extraction does not say the REX DCS is made for rope or high-angle rescue, so I did not use it.
SAND TIRES: our page has 4 Sand Tire variants ($4,305), but the Rapid Extraction accessories page says sand wheels "cannot be used with RexDCS" (the older brochure lists sand tires under the DCS). I left sand tires out of the copy. Please check with Rapid Extraction before keeping these variants.
SIZE: our page says 75”×18” assembled and 25”×18” folded; the Rapid Extraction DCS page and Bound Tree say 75”×24” and 25”×24”; the brochure says 75”×26” deployed and 25”×18” folded. I left the sizes out until you confirm.
WEIGHT: the Rapid Extraction DCS page, Bound Tree, and our page say 42 lbs; the REX overview brochure says "approx. 48 lbs." I left the weight out, as on the REX ONE page. I suggest 42 lbs.
Tire size: our page says 20” all-terrain tires; the DCS page and Bound Tree give no size. I left the size out.
META DESCRIPTION: the current one is for a different brand ("Low prices and fast shipping on Raine and other top tactical gear brands..."). The new one replaces it.
Duplicate content: our current description is the REX ONE text from the Rapid Extraction website with one DCS line added, and it still calls the frame "RexONE." The new copy is fully rewritten.
Price: standard tires $3,450 ($285 more than the REX ONE), sand tires $4,305; no compare-at price. Bound Tree lists the RexONE DCS at $4,359.99 (Blue) and $4,577.99 (Red). No change made.
Shipping weight: all 8 variants are set to 75 lbs. Is that the boxed weight?
Collections: the REX DCS is only in the Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection. Should it also go in Public Safety Gear, like the REX ONE?
Left out: "does the work of 4 to 6 responders," custom colors, and the patent number.
Images: the page has only one image. Would you like me to add Rapid Extraction photos (hand brake, descending stairs, treatment cot)? The current image alt text is the old product title.
